what_is_shared: The pair {MapStash, UniqueStash} as the tab types whose children are substashes
why_this_class: GGG tab type strings; the substash path /stash/{league}/{id}/{sub} is ground-truth Appendix A row (network-ground-truth.md:1081). C++ uses the pair to hide children from the tab list and gate them behind settings; Rust uses it to pick FetchSubstash vs FetchTab

what_is_shared: Folder children arrive in the top-level stash list; Map/Unique children arrive only in the parent tab fetch reply
why_this_class: API response shape. Handling diverges: C++ accepts children from a Folder reply (cpp:1014), Rust never fetches folders (plan lib.rs:797, SkipReason::Folder)

what_is_shared: Stash fetch addressed by (realm, league, id, optional substash id); character fetch addressed by name
why_this_class: Endpoint shapes (ground-truth Appendix A). Rust keys characters by GGG id and addresses by listed name (plan lib.rs:86); C++ keys and addresses by name/id differently
Documented GGG character fields. Rust has 6 (adds guardian, skills) in a different order; see tables.tsv
GGG item field. C++ recurses and gives a socketed item its host location; Rust lifts each into its own row with a socketed_in column (schema.sql:99)

what_is_shared: A parent tab fetch is authoritative for its substash membership: children it no longer lists are dropped/retired
why_this_class: Same rule, forced by the API (children are only visible in the parent reply). C++: in-memory EraseSourcesIf over FetchSourceKey + stashChildrenReplaced signal; Rust: SQL UPDATE ... removed_at keyed on listed_response. No shared structure

what_is_shared: A fresh stash/character listing is authoritative: tabs/characters it omits lose their items
why_this_class: Obvious reconciliation idea. C++ rebuilds m_tabs and erases buckets; Rust stamps listed_response then retires unstamped rows, keeps rows with removed_at, writes item_events, and keeps orphaned substash rows (no C++ analogue)

what_is_shared: A newly discovered tab is not fetched in the same pass
why_this_class: C++ F55: partial refresh leaves new tabs unfetched until full/explicit selection; Rust: binding plans, new tabs wait for the next plan. Different reasons and mechanism

what_is_shared: A substash item is attributed to its parent tab for display/pricing
why_this_class: C++ id()=parent, fetch_id=child; Rust keeps the substash as its own row with parent and reads the parent name/public for the game side (C80). Different decomposition

what_is_shared: The literal suffix "(Remove-only)" on a tab name
why_this_class: Game-written text (T11). C++ sets m_removeonly via endsWith and skips refresh locks (itemsmanager.cpp PropagateTabBuyouts); Rust has no remove-only flag at all, it tolerates trailing text generically; the string appears in Rust only in tests/fixtures

what_is_shared: Forum [linkItem location="Stash<n>" league x y realm] and character variant
why_this_class: Forum markup (T7). Attribute order differs (C++ location,league,x,y,realm; Rust realm,location,league,x,y) and n differs (C++ API index+1; Rust rank among website-listed tabs, T24). Strictly the pricing pair; noted for completeness

C++ GetLegacyHash "stash:"+label / "character:"+name, operator< stash-before-character, sort by tab index / locale-lowercased name, GetRect/QuadStash pixels: none reproduced. Rust identity is (realm, league, kind, id); character order is league, level desc, name (lib.rs:1681); tab order TAB_ORDER_KEYS (lib.rs:695)

C++ TabSelection All/Checked/Selected/TabsOnly, buyout-driven refresh checks, counters, stop tokens, Parse-skip, get_map_stashes/get_unique_stashes settings, 10-char id warning, realm/league character filter: none in Rust.
